mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of inflation and policy tightening, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average while personal income (PAYEMS) grows below its 5-year average signals a shift from consumption to precautionary savings, implying weaker demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-yr average AND PAYEMS < 5-yr average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 persons for three consecutive months despite an unemployment rate below 6% signals a labor market mismatch or underutilization, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 AND UNRATE < 6% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000 units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
